Action Plan:
1) Offer initial tests to investigate lower abdominal pain (urine testing and pregnancy test discussed). Patient preferred empiric treatment first.
2) Start empiric antibiotic for suspected urinary tract infection: Trimethoprim 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (dose/strength not documented). E-prescription sent to patient’s nominated pharmacy; start today.
3) Perform a pregnancy test to exclude pregnancy given pelvic pain and contraceptive implant use (patient advised to complete a test).
4) Symptomatic care: use paracetamol for pain as needed (dose not documented), maintain good oral hydration, consider cranberry juice.
5) Safety-netting: return/seek urgent care if worsening abdominal pain, persistent/high fever or feeling very hot/sweaty, vomiting, or if symptoms do not improve within a few days.
6) Follow-up: contact the clinic in a few days if no improvement or sooner if any red flags occur.
7) Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Chief complaint: Lower abdominal (suprapubic, below umbilicus) pain and feeling hot/sweaty.
- HPI:
  - Onset/duration: ~2 days; gradual onset; constant; worsening.
  - Quality/location: Burning pain, localized below the umbilicus; tender on pressure; no radiation.
  - Associated urinary symptoms: Increased urinary frequency; noted pink urine (possible hematuria); no dysuria or stinging; no flank pain reported.
  - GI: Mild nausea; no vomiting; constipation last week now resolved; no diarrhea.
  - Systemic: Feels hot/sweaty; temperature not measured.
- Gynecologic/sexual history:
  - Sexually active with one partner; last intercourse 4 days ago.
  - Contraception: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) inserted ~1 year ago.
  - Menses: Still having periods; LMP ~2 weeks ago.
  - STI screen: Negative ~6 months ago.
- Past medical history: Generally well.
- Surgical history: No prior surgeries.
- Medications: Implanon (etonogestrel implant). No other regular medications.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Family history: Non-contributory per patient.
- Social history: Lives in a shared house with two roommates; works as an accountant; non-smoker; drinks alcohol socially.

Objective:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Physical exam: Not performed/recorded in this consult.
- Investigations: None performed during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Lower abdominal pain with urinary frequency and pink urine (possible hematuria):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (DDx: High likelihood).
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Urolithiasis (distal ureter/bladder stone) (DDx: Medium) — supports: pink urine, frequency; opposes: pain not colicky, no flank pain.
     - Early appendicitis (DDx: Medium) — supports: gradual worsening pain, mild nausea/subjective fever; opposes: midline suprapubic location, no migration or peritoneal signs, no vomiting.
     - Early pregnancy-related complication, including ectopic (DDx: Low) — needs exclusion due to pelvic pain and reproductive age; on implant and no bleeding.
     - Pelvic inflammatory disease (DDx: Low) — less likely without discharge, dyspareunia, or STI risk features.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Pregnancy test recommended to exclude pregnancy.
     - No urinalysis/culture or imaging arranged today per patient preference (empiric treatment trial).
   - Treatment planned:
     - Trimethoprim: 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (dose/strength not documented); e-prescription sent; start today.
     - Paracetamol as needed for pain (dose not documented).
     - Hydration; may try cranberry juice.
     - Safety-netting: return/urgent care if worsening pain, persistent/high fever or feeling very hot/sweaty, vomiting, or lack of improvement within a few days.
   - Relevant referrals: None at this time.

2. Pregnancy status clarification:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Pregnancy status unknown; on etonogestrel implant; LMP ~2 weeks ago.
   - Differential diagnosis: Early pregnancy-related complication (including ectopic) (DDx: Low) — to be excluded.
   - Investigations planned: Perform a pregnancy test.
   - Treatment planned: None specific pending test result.
   - Relevant referrals: None at this time.

  - Allergies not documented.
  - No vital signs recorded.
  - No physical abdominal/urinary or pelvic exam findings documented.
  - No urinalysis or urine culture obtained before antibiotics.
  - Medication strengths/doses for trimethoprim and paracetamol not documented.
